name: CRC Calculator
blurb: CRC-8/16/32 with polynomial, init and reflection settings
intro: Computes a CRC over text or hex bytes with the Rocksoft parameter model (width, polynomial, init, reflect in/out, xor out). Pick a catalogue preset or set your own; every preset is also run on the same data so you can find which one a device uses, and C code is generated for the chosen one.

inputs.label: Data
inputs.help: Text, text with C escapes (\r\n, \x02) or hex bytes, as chosen below.

inputs.label: Known CRC (hex), to identify
inputs.help: Optional: a CRC you already have for this data. The presets that give it (as written or byte-swapped) are named.

examples.title: Modbus RTU frame: read 2 holding registers from slave 1

usage: Give data as text, escaped text or hex bytes (format = text | escaped | hex) and a preset name, or preset = custom with width (8/16/32), poly, init and xorout as hex strings and refin/refout as booleans. Optionally give expect = a known CRC (hex) to list the catalogue presets that produce it over the data. Returns the CRC in hex and decimal, its bytes in both orders, the check value over "123456789", the CRC under every catalogue preset, and C code. Use it to verify a protocol checksum or to identify which CRC variant a device uses. result.crc holds the chosen parameters and the CRC as numbers.
sources: Ross N. Williams, A Painless Guide to CRC Error Detection Algorithms (1993), the Rocksoft model
Greg Cook, Catalogue of parametrised CRC algorithms (CRC RevEng), check values
Modbus over Serial Line V1.02, section 6.2.2 (CRC-16 low byte first)
